thread.title: Retirement Strategy: I Am Done Being Wrong About This Market

author: Regarded Solutions
title: Retirement Strategy: I Am Done Being Wrong About This Market
text:
I have been banging the drum about a market correction, but I suppose I just might croak waiting for one. The bottom line is that I have been wrong or early. Being early is still being wrong, folks, and I won't hide from the facts.
Let's take a peek at where the markets have been and where they have gone:
^DJI data by YCharts
After the drop in January/February, the Dow has moved basically sideways and rebounded off of its lows several times. It appears that the bottom was support. Since I made the conscience decision to build cash and not buy or sell any stocks, I could say that I missed some good opportunities. At the same time, I didn't sell anything and the dividend income stream continued to rise.
As illustrated by the model Dividend King Retirement Portfolio , the dividend income stream moved higher, while the price fluctuations had no effect on the income. Of course, if I had deployed more cash, the portfolio would have more shares and an even greater income stream.
The model DKRP currently consists of Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO ), Procter & Gamble (NYSE: PG ), Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ ), 3M (NYSE: MMM ), Emerson Electric (NYSE: EMR ), Cincinnati Financial Corp. (NASDAQ: CINF ), Lowe's (NYSE: LOW ), Hormel (NYSE: HRL ), Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE: CL ), Dover (NYSE: DOV ), and AT&T (NYSE: T ).
Here is the chart that shows the dividend trajectory over the last 3 years:
Dividends Paid (TTM) data by YCharts
A smooth, boring increase without breaking a sweat. Damn the torpedoes, full steam ahead - or actually - Ignore the price fluctuations and keep on investing ! Well, I wish I were that cavalier about it at my stage, but I will emphasize once again that the more time you have (10+ years before retirement), the more you might want to just keep plugging away.
Maybe I was being too cute. Maybe I should have taken the same action as before and bought the dips. As a retired guy, I made the decision not to put more cash at risk and wait for the "big one" to pick up some extreme bargains in quality Dividend Champion stocks.
While I have missed the call thus far, I took what I believed to be the correct action to take. My circumstances led me to my decision. This is where I stand right now:
I have more cash than ever before. While the income stream did increase, there has been no exponential growth in terms of owning more shares. The portfolio has remained static but has not lost a dime. All Is Not As It Appears Though I won't reiterate my conservative position, but even though the tax cuts have been better for corporate profits than I ever expected and have moved many valuations into "reasonable levels," I still believe we need to be vigilant about what might be ahead.
Take a look at this chart of the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq:
^SPX data by YCharts
The S&P 500 is just 4% off of its all-time high and is actually up for the year. The Nasdaq is at an all-time high, as well as being up for the year too! That being said, did you know that about 27% of the Nasdaq consists of the FAANG stocks: Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ), Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ) and Google (NASDAQ: GOOGL )? Take a look at this chart from Bloomberg:
These stocks also account for an amazing 11% of the S&P 500:
I can make a pretty good case that as "FAANG" goes, so go the markets. As of now, only AAPL pays a dividend and is not a Champion yet (I believe it will be a "King" decades from now, by the way).
I suppose what I am saying is that if the market is being held up by just 5 stocks, there are still wolves (or bears) in the woods. Therefore, I will continue to be more conservative.
I Will Be Conservative And Vigilant, But Growing Cash Is Over! Yes, you read that correctly. Even though I am a retired old guy, I am tweaking my approach right now and will look for stocks to add to the model portfolio or to add shares of existing positions. (BTW, that means my personal portfolio as well.)
Here is what I will be looking at:
A dividend "opportunity" stock to add some gusto to the model portfolio. I am thinking of Annaly Capital (NYSE: NLY ), with its recent drop in share price, its dividend yield, and the fact that mortgage rates are higher:
NLY data by YCharts
Adding shares of MMM because of the price drop, the easing of trade tensions, and an "accidentally" higher yield:
MMM data by YCharts
Adding shares of JNJ, for the same reasons as MMM:
JNJ data by YCharts
I intend on taking small bites of these and will let you know the details when I do it. There will be others that I will be looking into, but these stocks are what I will begin with.
Before I Make Any Moves, I Want Your Input First Prior to just diving in, I would really love to know what great dividend stocks you believe should be purchased. My articles get plenty of comments, and you folks just might give everyone, including me, food for thought!
Let me hear from you !
